uncited: The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation defines a primitive $i$ by its position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $\mathbf{c}_i$ (often represented via spherical harmonics) [Parent].
where $\sigma_i = \alpha_i G'_i(x')$ and $G'_i(x')$ is the 2D Gaussian kernel evaluated at pixel $x'$ [Parent].
All methods in this family retain the differentiable rendering framework of 3D Gaussian Splatting [Parent].

**Primitive Attributes:** Modifying the allowed values or constraints of primitive parameters, such as allowing $\mathbf{c}_i$ to take negative values ([Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md)) or constraining $\mathbf{p}_i$ to a structured grid ([Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md)).
**Kernel Function:** Replacing the exponential Gaussian kernel with other decaying functions of the Mahalanobis distance ([DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md)).

**Geometric Constraints:** Enforcing spatial relationships during densification, such as placing new primitives on the tangent plane of existing ones ([GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md)) or wrapping primitives around surfaces ([Gaussian Wrapping](#gaussian-wrapping)).
**Rendering Pipeline:** Injecting differentiable blur kernels into the rasterization step to model spatially-varying defocus ([Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md)).
Choose this method when high-fidelity human avatar reconstruction with complex garments is needed.
Choose this method when extracting watertight meshes from thin structures or surface geometry is the primary goal.
Choose this method when compressing kernel-modulated neural representations for light field or view-dependent rendering.
The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation [Parent] assumes symmetric, positive-definite Gaussians with positive opacity and color.
Negative Gaussian Splatting and Gaussian Wrapping address the inability of standard Gaussians to represent voids or sharp surface boundaries.
Scaffold-GS and GeoGaussian address the unstructured nature of standard Gaussians, which can lead to redundancy or geometric inconsistency.
DARBF-Splatting and Grid-based Blur Kernels address the mathematical rigidity of the Gaussian kernel, allowing for more flexible shape modeling and blur handling.
